subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should fenced final-reply `MEDIA:` tokens stay non-delivered with one outbound delivery warning, or should OpenClaw extract standalone valid `MEDIA:` tokens from code fences?
rationale: Current source intentionally preserves fenced examples as text, but the reported failure is silent media loss; extraction could turn legitimate code examples into attachments, while warn-only leaves delivery semantics unchanged.

options.title: Land Warn-Only Diagnostics
options.body: Review and land the linked warn-only PR shape so fenced tokens remain visible text but emit one warning at the actual delivery boundary.

options.title: Extract Fenced Tokens
options.body: Change the parser contract to deliver valid standalone fenced `MEDIA:` lines, accepting the risk that examples can become attachments.

options.title: Document As By Design
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and rely on documentation and prompt guidance, leaving runtime skips silent unless another diagnostic path is added.

recommendation.title: Land Warn-Only Diagnostics
recommendation.body: Review and land the linked warn-only PR shape so fenced tokens remain visible text but emit one warning at the actual delivery boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the current review direction on the linked PR and have recent release-path history on the affected parser behavior.
